chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: High school and limited work around Homestead
summary: She finished high school in the late 1920s with little to do afterward in town.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How far through high school did you go?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

I finished high school but there wasn't that much to do around Homestead. I waited tables -- one of my aunts had a restaurant, one of my great-aunts -- my grandmother on my father's side had two sisters and a brother and they all had some sort of little business -- a restaurant or a little, what they call -- well, my grandmother had the barber shop and had hat cleaning, etc., and I think the other girls had boarding and rooming houses, so when I came out of school I just worked in one of my aunt's restaurants until, I guess, until Harry came back and then I guess that's when I started singing around. But I wasn't working at it. But in those days I wasn't doing much work anyway. There wasn't much to do and I don't suppose we felt that we needed that much. Things were pretty cheap in those days so you could manage pretty well.
So now we're talking about the late 1920s when you graduated from high school.
